pull.title: kernel: document that btck_WriteBytes may receive a null pointer
pull.body:
The header does not say whether the bytes pointer can be null when size is zero. It can: `btck_witness_stack_get_item_at` passes `std::vector::data()` straight through, and that may be null for an empty element.

An alternative is to guarantee non-null rather than document that it isn't. In other words, route the vector-backed writer calls through a helper that substitutes a valid, never-read pointer when the buffer is empty.

comments.body:
Documenting how callers should deal with this seems out of scope, would just describe behaviour. Let's also use more complete Doxygen syntax while we're at it.

<details>
<summary>git diff on 76359bee61</summary>

```diff
diff --git a/src/kernel/bitcoinkernel.h b/src/kernel/bitcoinkernel.h
index ba6daf72fd..0ada5576a9 100644
--- a/src/kernel/bitcoinkernel.h
+++ b/src/kernel/bitcoinkernel.h
@@ -391,11 +391,11 @@ typedef void (*btck_ValidationInterfaceBlockDisconnected)(void* user_data, btck_
 /**
  * Function signature for serializing data.
  *
- * The bytes pointer may be null when size is zero. Callers that construct a
- * language-level slice or array view from the arguments must handle that
- * case, as some languages require a non-null pointer even for an empty view.
- *
- * Returns 0 to indicate success.
+ * @param[in] bytes    The data to write. Can be null if size is 0.
+ * @param[in] size     The number of bytes in the data.
+ * @param[in] userdata Holds the user-defined opaque structure that was given
+ *                     with the writer.
+ * @return             0 on success.
  */
 typedef int (*btck_WriteBytes)(const void* bytes, size_t size, void* userdata);
 

```
</details>

The commit message in 76359be says that this is relevant only to bindings, but I think it also matters to C users, for example when they give `bytes` to `memcpy`. I suggest this more general alternative:

```
kernel: document that btck_WriteBytes may receive a null pointer

btck_witness_stack_get_item_at passes std::vector::data() to the writer,
which can be null for an empty witness item. Document this in the contract,
together with the other btck_WriteBytes parameters.
```
